label: first copy-phase step after <DEL> in short (L=3) sequences
explanation: Fires almost exclusively at recall_idx == 1 (the step right after <DEL>, input = first original token, output = second original token) in short sequences: L=3 (~73% of such steps fire, 78% of activation mass, all top activations) and more weakly/selectively L=4 (~9% of such steps, 22% of mass). Essentially silent in the original phase, at the delimiter, at later copy steps, and for L>=5. Within L=3/4 the magnitude depends on token identity (higher when output/next tokens are f, b, p, 3, l, 2; lower for 0, 1, n, m, w, e; fewer digits in the sequence -> more active), but no simple token rule improved F1. Predicate (recall_idx==1)&(L<=4) gets ~100% recall but 19% precision; L==3 alone is the best F1 tradeoff.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the input two steps back (most: l, 3, 2, p, o, b; least: y, t, u, e) and the next token to output (most: 3, p, l, b, f, 2; least: t, e, w, n); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=4, L=3, recall_idx=1.
